<p>When you visit a gynecologist, the first question you are asked is always the same: "When was your last period?". At this moment, many women frantically search their memory, giving approximate dates or hesitating with "it was the beginning of the month, maybe the middle." Most women only feel the need to track their menstrual cycle in two cases: when they want to get pregnant or when they want to avoid pregnancy.</p><p>But the truth is that the menstrual cycle is the "fifth vital sign" of the female body (along with pulse, temperature, blood pressure, and respiration). It is not just bleeding days, but a monthly health report your body sends you. Recording these days in a notebook is a thing of the past. In the modern era, smart apps like "Anacan" solve this process in seconds. Why should every woman track her cycle? Let's look at 3 main health benefits.</p><h2>1. Early Diagnosis: Seeing Your Body's "SOS" Signals</h2><p>The menstrual cycle is a mirror of your hormones. If sudden changes occur in your cycle, this could be the first sign of hidden internal problems. When you track regularly, you know what is "normal." The Anacan app helps you notice the following deviations in time:</p><ul><li><strong>Cycle length changes:</strong> If your cycle suddenly shortens (less than 21 days) or lengthens (more than 35 days), this could be a harbinger of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS), thyroid problems, or hormonal imbalance.</li><li><strong>Spotting:</strong> Bleeding between periods can indicate problems like polyps or fibroids.</li><li><strong>Severity of pain:</strong> By recording the level of pain in the app, you can see if it worsens over time (suspicion of Endometriosis).</li></ul><p>Through the app, you can notice these "abnormalities" immediately rather than months later and consult a doctor.</p><h2>2. Managing PMS and Mood Swings</h2><p>Has it ever happened that you got angry for no reason, cried, or wanted to scream at everyone, and then 2 days passed and your period started? You felt relieved saying, "Aha, so that's why!". Premenstrual Syndrome (PMS) is a nightmare for many women. But if you know "when the enemy is coming," you can prepare for it. With the "Anacan" app:</p><ul><li><strong>Forecast:</strong> The app warns you that the PMS period is approaching.</li><li><strong>Preparation:</strong> You know that your energy might be low next week or you will be more sensitive. Therefore, you can postpone important meetings, be more understanding of yourself, or replace sweet cravings with healthy alternatives.</li><li><strong>Symptom Tracking:</strong> By noting headaches, breast swelling, or acne, you can see the patterns that repeat every month.</li></ul><h2>3. Accurate Communication with the Doctor and Correct Treatment</h2><p>Instead of guessing "What date was it last month?" when going to the doctor, taking out your phone and providing accurate information is half the diagnosis. The "Anacan" app acts as your digital health card. You can show the doctor not only the last date but also the following details:</p><ul><li>Cycle length and regularity of the last 6 months.</li><li>Amount of bleeding (heavy or light).</li><li>On which days the pain started.</li><li>Days of sexual intercourse (for those planning pregnancy).</li></ul><p>This precise information helps the doctor get to the root of the problem directly without ordering unnecessary tests.</p><h2>Why "Anacan"?</h2><p>Although there are many tracker apps in the global market, Anacan is specially designed for Azerbaijani women:</p><ul><li><strong>In our native language:</strong> There is no need to translate medical terms with a dictionary.</li><li><strong>Local content:</strong> It provides advice suitable for our climate, dietary habits, and lifestyle.</li><li><strong>Privacy:</strong> Your data is protected securely.</li></ul><p>Keeping a menstrual calendar is not just about marking red days, it is about respecting your body and learning its language.
